ninth.title: The Ninth, under examination
ninth.intro: Both writers resist the authority of Beethoven’s reputation. Their reservations about the Ninth do not amount to the same argument.
ninth.scope: Includes a footnote in Hanslick’s Chapter III and Tolstoy’s Chapter XVI.

annotations.label: Object
annotations.title: What is being judged?
annotations.copy: Hanslick makes the finale the point at issue, while praising the first three movements with a qualification. Tolstoy asks the entire work to meet his criterion of good art. The objects of their judgments overlap without being identical.
phrases: it is the Finale which is the point at issue
Beethoven’s Ninth Symphony is considered a great work of art.

annotations.label: Criterion
annotations.title: Two tests of the same celebrated work.
annotations.copy: Hanslick distinguishes a noble intention from musical beauty. Tolstoy asks whether the work can unite people beyond an audience trained to receive it. Agreement in disapproval conceals a difference in what could count as a defence.
phrases: the quality of uniting all men in one common feeling

annotations.label: Concession
annotations.title: Keep the admissions in view.
annotations.copy: Hanslick acknowledges genius and individuality in the very passage where he denies beauty. Tolstoy allows comprehensible snatches within what he condemns as a whole. Their concessions narrow the targets; they do not erase the force of either judgment.
phrases: except short snatches which are lost in a sea of what is incomprehensible

ninth.method: Hanslick places this discussion in a long footnote to his argument about music and language. It is easy to miss if one reads only the main text. The complete note continues on page 97, where he discusses Strauss and Becher; the source visit preserves that setting. Tolstoy’s paragraph follows his division of Christian art into religious and universal kinds.
ninth.limit: This is an editorial comparison of two printed arguments, not evidence of a conversation between the writers. Neither excerpt proves how the symphony acts on every listener. No recording is supplied: the study examines their stated criteria, and the score has rights separate from any performance.
